stages.reconstruct: Glass→air higher-to-lower n permits critical angle. Below i_c Snell has propagating r and partial reflection; above i_c no propagating transmitted ray, ideal TIR.

core1b.fresh_task: Core n=1.6, cladding n=1.2. A ray strikes boundary at i=55°. Will TIR occur? Then replace cladding with n=1.4.
core1b.protected_work: Calculate critical-angle admissibility and apply it to a changed surrounding medium.

stages.reconstruct: i_c=arcsin(.75)≈48.6°, so yes initially. New i_c=arcsin(.875)≈61.0°, 55° below threshold, no TIR.

stages.repair: Use n_lower/n_higher and incidence to normal, then test strict inequality.
stages.boundary_test: If cladding index equals core index, can TIR guide rays at the boundary?

stages.predict: State your expected result, direction or relationship before solving. Record uncertainty if needed.
stages.attempt: A student says TIR occurs whenever sin i≥n₂/n₁ for any pair of media. Derive and qualify the statement.
stages.reconstruct: Snell gives sin r=(n₁/n₂)sin i. Need n₁>n₂ for sub-90° critical. Strict i>i_c gives no propagating transmitted ray; equality is grazing limiting direction. Ideal assumptions matter.
stages.diagnose: Only if your saved answer demonstrates this error: Treating index ordering as sufficient or critical equality as ordinary above-threshold case. Otherwise record insufficient evidence; compare your actual reasoning with the reconstruction.
stages.repair: Derive sine domain and compare both conditions.
stages.boundary_test: What changes when the incident side is air and outgoing side glass?
